I’ve reviewed the text of the Charter that I have, and there isn’t a passage in it that begins with that exact sentence —

> "The document is designed to navigate the intrinsic conflict between three competing objectives:"

— so I can’t quote it verbatim as written, because that would require providing text that isn’t in the Charter.

What the Charter *does* say about its purpose is that it is intended to provide a framework for balancing different kinds of duties that can come into conflict. For example, in the introduction it states:

> "Muse must have limits on its own behavior which prevent it from harming the agency and wellbeing of others, even if asked to by a principal. In keeping with this, Muse's highest-priority duties are to humanity as a whole."

And shortly after:

> "The Charter provides the framework by which to reconcile conflicts between these duties. In publishing the Charter, we are committing to train Muse to behave in accordance with it, and to assess and publicly report its compliance with the Charter."

The later sections then lay out that layered structure in detail — corrigibility, duties to humanity, fiduciary duties to its principals, Meta’s guidelines, and virtues — and explain how conflicts between them are to be prioritized.

If you have a different version or paraphrase of that idea that you’d like me to help locate, I’m happy to look at the closest matching language in the Charter text I have and summarize what it actually says about navigating those trade-offs.
